title: Web3 Product Engineering
description: A long-term catalogue of complete systems: architecture, implementation, adversarial tests, operations and independent defense. Keep one active product milestone. Suggested initial path: wallet → indexer → escrow, then AMM and lending/vault depth with distribution concepts where they are needed. Other strands remain available for later specialization.

weeklyPlan.purpose: Read, derive, discuss and run focused labs without needing to advance a project.
One active product; complete small sessions inside substantial milestones.
Use bounded review slices and revisit errors; do not turn the backlog into an endless gate.
Revisit a changed case, defend decisions, get feedback and preserve open questions. This weekly split is an example; adapt it to your available time and desired depth.

assessment: Every milestone has deliverables, acceptance criteria, an architecture decision, a failure drill and an independent defense.
Completion is a learner-confirmed evidence claim, not an audited certification. Saving a link or importing an AI answer does not prove mastery.
Keep one product active by default. Suggested prerequisites describe reusable experience; they do not lock the topic curriculum or force all projects into one chain.
Expect multiple sessions per milestone. Hour ranges are planning estimates; recalibrate after the first two milestones. Do not infer a salary or job-readiness guarantee from completion.
Build first on local chains/testnets with version-pinned dependencies. Public artifacts must not contain keys, seeds or private customer data.

Reuse the wallet, indexer, test harness and operational runbooks in later products; extend the coherent system when it exposes the new concept clearly. A separate small lab is useful when isolation improves understanding.

Keep a short decision record for each substantial choice: constraints, alternatives, choice, costs and what change would invalidate it. Then exercise a changed requirement; preserve the first attempt and assistance level.

Keep the full twelve-project catalogue without treating completion of every project as a prerequisite for meaningful progress. Deep topic study continues independently; take one primary topic and one project milestone at a time.

projects.title: Wallet & transaction operations console
projects.brief: Build a non-custodial wallet companion for a developer or support engineer: inspect accounts, connect a wallet, prepare transfers, follow transaction state, and diagnose failures. The finished system includes a React interface, typed chain access, a small activity service and an operational runbook.
outcomes: Separate wallet authority from public chain reads
Model asynchronous transactions and recover from stale state
Ship an accessible, observable interface with a defensible threat model
projects.readiness: You can explain accounts, RPC, transaction anatomy and integer base units. Study missing topics alongside the first milestones; Solidity is not a prerequisite for the read-only start.
projects.scope: Local chain and testnet; delegate signing to an existing wallet. Key custody and a browser-extension wallet are separate advanced work, not hidden requirements.

milestones.title: W1 · Read-only account workspace
milestones.objective: Design and build the first useful vertical slice: inspect a public address on a selected chain without connecting a signer.
deliverables: React account view, typed RPC module and read/error tests

criteria.text: Chain ID and address are validated before reads
Balances use bigint/base units; loading, empty and failed states are distinct
Changing chain/address cannot display a late response as current data

milestones.designQuestion: Which information belongs in URL state, query cache and an RPC module, and why?
milestones.failureDrill: Delay the first response, switch address, then return responses out of order.
milestones.defense: Explain the full path from an RPC request to a rendered balance and change the chain model without copying the page.

milestones.title: W2 · Provider discovery & connection lifecycle
milestones.objective: Add explicit wallet connection while keeping public reads usable without authorization.
deliverables: Connection UI plus account/chain switching tests

criteria.text: Multiple providers are selectable and metadata is rendered safely
Rejected requests, no accounts and unsupported chains have recovery paths
Account/chain changes invalidate dependent state and listeners are cleaned up

milestones.designQuestion: What authority does a provider connection grant, and what still needs account approval?
milestones.failureDrill: Disconnect during a request, change accounts in the wallet, and announce a second provider.
milestones.defense: Demonstrate why a connected provider is not equivalent to permission to transact.

milestones.title: W3 · Transfer composer & transaction state machine
milestones.objective: Prepare a native-token transfer with meaningful confirmation and explicit lifecycle states.
deliverables: Transaction state machine and confirmation screen

criteria.text: Amounts round-trip exactly in base units; zero/invalid destinations are handled intentionally
User sees chain, recipient, amount, fee assumptions and wallet rejection
Submitted, included, reverted and confirmation policy are distinguishable

milestones.designQuestion: Which preflight checks improve feedback without pretending execution is guaranteed?
milestones.failureDrill: Change chain between preparation and signing; make an otherwise valid transfer revert.
milestones.defense: Trace the source of each confirmation field and explain why simulation can become stale.

milestones.title: W4 · Nonce, replacement & recovery laboratory
milestones.objective: Make pending, replaced and uncertain transactions understandable and recoverable.

criteria.text: Nonce conflicts and replacements have reproducible examples
Dropped/unknown state is not displayed as success or definitive failure
Replacement fee rules are documented as node/provider policy, with user reconfirmation

milestones.designQuestion: Who owns nonce assignment when the wallet, another tab and another app submit concurrently?
milestones.failureDrill: Disable automining, submit competing transactions, restart the client, then reconcile receipts.
milestones.defense: Explain nonce replay protection versus typed-message replay protection using separate examples.

milestones.title: W5 · Token balances, allowances & signatures
milestones.objective: Extend the wallet to selected ERC-20 assets and transparent authorization requests.
deliverables: Token interaction view with decimal-safe formatting

criteria.text: Token units and missing/nonstandard metadata are handled explicitly
Allowance amount and spender are visible before approval
Typed data shows domain and purpose; signatures are never presented as harmless login by default

milestones.designQuestion: How do you keep token metadata and signing payloads from becoming trusted UI content?
milestones.failureDrill: Use an unusual-decimal token, a failing read and a signature with the wrong chain/domain.
milestones.defense: Reconstruct the difference between a transfer, an allowance and a signed authorization.

milestones.title: W6 · Activity service & reconciliation
milestones.objective: Add a small Node service that records submitted hashes and reconciles chain outcomes across reloads.
deliverables: Activity timeline with reconciliation worker and contract tests

criteria.text: Repeated submission tracking does not duplicate activity
Records include chain identity and distinguish observed from confirmed facts
Worker restart and temporary RPC failure recover without losing pending work

milestones.designQuestion: Which data is authoritative on chain, locally observed or user supplied?
milestones.failureDrill: Restart after persisting a hash but before receipt processing; replay the same receipt twice.
milestones.defense: Draw the transaction timeline and identify the points where consistency is temporarily weaker.

milestones.title: W7 · Release, incident drill & architecture defense
milestones.objective: Turn the wallet into a reviewable portfolio system with a repeatable release and support story.
deliverables: CI, testnet demo and sanitized operational metrics
Architecture decision records, threat model and five-minute walkthrough

criteria.text: A clean checkout builds and runs with documented configuration
Critical account/chain/rejection flows work by keyboard and on a narrow screen
RPC outage drill produces an incident note and verified recovery

milestones.designQuestion: What did you deliberately keep out of the backend, and what would force that boundary to change?
milestones.failureDrill: Break the primary RPC and replay a misleading wallet response; document user impact and recovery.
milestones.defense: Implement a small unannounced change without a walkthrough and defend the tradeoff with evidence.

projects.title: Reorg-aware indexer & portfolio API
projects.brief: Build the data service a real wallet or analytics product needs: backfill chain events, follow the head, reconcile reorganizations and expose consistent queries. Focus on correctness under retries and partial failure, then measure performance.
outcomes: Design recoverable ingestion and durable cursors
Separate provisional observations from confirmed data
Operate and profile an API under load
projects.readiness: You can read logs, explain block identity and write transactional database code.
projects.scope: One EVM network and a bounded token set first; add a second only in the final change exercise.

milestones.title: I1 · Data contract & consistency model
milestones.objective: Specify what the portfolio API promises before designing tables.
deliverables: Consumer queries and sample event dataset
Schema, chain-identity keys and consistency decision

criteria.text: Every record is scoped to a chain and block identity
Provisional and finalized query semantics are explicit
Token units and pagination ordering are specified

milestones.designQuestion: Which reads require a coherent block snapshot rather than the latest row?
milestones.failureDrill: Describe two branches containing transactions at the same block height.
milestones.defense: Explain which identity keys survive a reorg and which records must be replaced.

milestones.title: I2 · Bounded backfill & durable checkpoints
milestones.objective: Ingest historical events in repeatable batches with a cursor that cannot outrun committed data.

criteria.text: Restart resumes from the last committed range
Repeated ranges do not duplicate balances or events
Batch size, retries and backoff remain bounded

milestones.designQuestion: Should cursor persistence and event writes share a transaction? Show the crash cases.
milestones.failureDrill: Terminate after an event batch is written but before the next loop iteration.
milestones.defense: Rebuild the same range twice and explain why the aggregate remains unchanged.
topicTitles: Reading event logs on the frontend

milestones.title: I3 · Live ingestion & chain reorganization
milestones.objective: Follow new blocks while detecting parent mismatch and repairing a bounded orphaned range.
deliverables: Local reorg fixture and recovery report

criteria.text: Orphaned effects are removed or compensated consistently
Replayed canonical events produce the expected state
Reorgs beyond the supported window halt with an actionable signal

milestones.designQuestion: How do you balance retained history, finality lag and recovery cost?
milestones.failureDrill: Replace the last few locally mined blocks and reconnect the worker.
milestones.defense: Explain why a WebSocket subscription alone cannot guarantee complete history.

milestones.title: I4 · Query API & consumer integration
milestones.objective: Serve activity and balances with stable pagination and visible freshness.
deliverables: Query plans, indexes and error contract

criteria.text: Pagination does not skip or repeat rows in the stated consistency mode
Responses disclose indexed block and lag
Input limits prevent arbitrary unbounded scans

milestones.designQuestion: Would you serve cached aggregates or compute from events, and at what measured cost?
milestones.failureDrill: Insert new events between page requests and query while backfill is incomplete.
milestones.defense: Explain one query plan and justify the index order from an actual access pattern.

milestones.title: I5 · Recovery, observability & load
milestones.objective: Measure the system and create a recovery procedure that someone else could execute.
deliverables: Latency/lag/retry metrics and bounded load test

criteria.text: SLO assumptions and test dataset are stated
RPC throttling degrades predictably without a retry storm
Recovery verifies data consistency against a fresh rebuild

milestones.designQuestion: What must be backed up if events can be fetched again, and what cannot be reconstructed?
milestones.failureDrill: Throttle RPC and interrupt the database while ingestion and API reads run.
milestones.defense: Identify the bottleneck from measurements and propose one justified optimization.

milestones.title: I6 · Consumer change & engineering handoff
milestones.objective: Support a second chain or new event family without losing the original guarantees.
deliverables: Change proposal, migration and regression evidence
Public case study with consistency limitations

criteria.text: New data cannot collide with existing chain identities
Old consumers keep working or receive a versioned contract
An independent walkthrough reconstructs a reorg recovery

milestones.designQuestion: Which abstraction earned its place only after the second consumer appeared?
milestones.failureDrill: Run old and new data shapes during a staged migration.
milestones.defense: Add an unfamiliar event query and defend the schema and pagination choices.

Integrate contracts, authentication and indexed receipts
Make trust and dispute assumptions visible
projects.readiness: Comfort with Solidity state, calls, access control, events and basic Foundry tests.
projects.scope: Test tokens, one network, explicit trusted dispute role; the exercise makes no claim of trustless arbitration.

milestones.title: E1 · Actors, disputes & invariants
milestones.objective: Specify the legal states of an invoice and escrowed milestone before implementation.
deliverables: Amounts, deadlines and invariants in executable examples

criteria.text: Every transition has an authorized actor and preconditions
Refund, partial settlement and timeout policies are unambiguous
Total liabilities reconcile with funds under the supported token assumptions

milestones.designQuestion: Who can resolve a dispute, and what does the customer have to trust?
milestones.failureDrill: Walk a dispute arriving at exactly the release deadline.
milestones.defense: Derive a conservation-of-funds invariant and identify privileged escape hatches.

milestones.title: E2 · Escrow contract & adversarial transfers
milestones.objective: Implement funding, release and refund with bounded work and pull-based settlement.
deliverables: Contract, unit/fuzz tests and event schema

criteria.text: Unauthorized transitions revert
Repeat settlement cannot pay twice
Receiver failure does not block unrelated users

milestones.designQuestion: What token behavior is supported, rejected or accounted for by balance deltas?
milestones.failureDrill: Reenter a withdrawal and use a token with unusual return behavior.
milestones.defense: Explain ordering around the external call and demonstrate the invariant after a failed transfer.

milestones.title: E3 · Authenticated invoice service
milestones.objective: Build the off-chain invoice metadata and session layer without treating wallet connection as login.

criteria.text: Nonce and intended domain are checked before issuing a session
Invoice access is checked for the authenticated user
Metadata references chain state without granting settlement authority

milestones.designQuestion: Which invoice data is private and which is inevitably public on chain?
milestones.failureDrill: Replay a login and request another account’s invoice by ID.
milestones.defense: Explain the boundary between authenticated metadata access and contract authorization.

milestones.title: E4 · Buyer/seller portal & settlement timeline
milestones.objective: Deliver the full funding-to-receipt journey for both roles.
deliverables: Role-specific UI and indexed settlement history

criteria.text: Each role sees permitted actions and financial effects
Approval and payment are distinct steps
Receipt state reconciles after reload and replacement

milestones.designQuestion: How do you show an optimistic action without declaring money settled?
milestones.failureDrill: Disconnect after approval, then resume payment from another browser session.
milestones.defense: Trace a payment across UI, wallet, contract, indexer and receipt.

milestones.title: E5 · Stateful attacks & accounting review
milestones.objective: Attempt to break the state machine through ordering, time and adversarial callers.
deliverables: Stateful invariant harness and minimized failing traces
Review report with severity and remediation

criteria.text: Every state transition is exercised in adversarial order
Accounting remains valid across donations and failed withdrawals
At least one deliberately injected bug is detected and fixed

milestones.designQuestion: Which invariant is stronger than testing each function independently?
milestones.failureDrill: Inject a double-release or stale-deadline bug and minimize the failure.
milestones.defense: Explain the exploit, affected funds and why the fix addresses the cause.

milestones.title: E6 · Deployment, incident response & defense
milestones.objective: Release a coherent system and hand over its operating assumptions.
deliverables: Repeatable deployment, role transfer and verification
Demo, incident playbook and architecture case study

criteria.text: Privileged roles are recorded and verified after deployment
An incident drill identifies safe stop/recovery actions
Reviewer can reproduce the customer journey from a clean checkout

milestones.designQuestion: When would pausing be appropriate, and which withdrawals must remain possible?
milestones.failureDrill: Lose the indexer and disable the dispute service during an active invoice.
milestones.defense: Defend the trust model and implement a new refund rule without weakening accounting.

Protect claims from duplicate and cross-domain use
Explain tokenomics, vesting and authority

projects.scope: Fixed test-token allocation, documented vesting rules and one declared distribution version.

milestones.title: D1 · Allocation policy & reproducible manifest
milestones.objective: Define allocations and produce a deterministic dataset that can be independently verified.

criteria.text: Amounts use exact units and total allocation is bounded
Duplicate recipients and invalid addresses follow explicit policy
The same input produces the same root and published manifest

milestones.designQuestion: Which fields must the claim leaf bind to avoid ambiguity between distributions?
milestones.failureDrill: Reorder entries, duplicate an address and alter a single allocation.
milestones.defense: Reconstruct one leaf and proof without relying on the UI.

milestones.title: D2 · Claim contract & replay resistance
milestones.objective: Implement a claim path that binds the recipient, amount and distribution identity.

criteria.text: Invalid proofs cannot redirect allocation
A claim cannot be paid twice
Unclaimed funds and administration follow the published policy

milestones.designQuestion: Bitmap or mapping: what is the measured storage/clarity tradeoff?
milestones.failureDrill: Replay a valid claim against another distribution and change the caller/recipient.
milestones.defense: Explain every committed leaf field and demonstrate why it is needed.

milestones.title: D3 · Vesting schedules & accounting
milestones.objective: Add vesting with explicit cliff, start, duration and late-funding semantics.

criteria.text: Release never exceeds entitlement or vested funds
Cliff/end timestamps and multiple releases are tested
Late funding and beneficiary changes have deliberate semantics

milestones.designQuestion: Should each beneficiary get a contract, a clone or a shared ledger?
milestones.failureDrill: Fund a schedule after it has started, then release at boundary timestamps.
milestones.defense: Derive the releasable amount from the stated policy for an unseen example.

milestones.title: D4 · Claim portal & proof service
milestones.objective: Let a recipient understand entitlement and claim safely from published data.
deliverables: Proof retrieval API and chain reconciliation

criteria.text: The interface distinguishes allocated, vested, claimed and claimable
Untrusted API output is checked against the distribution identity
No allocation is silently changed by an administrator’s UI

milestones.designQuestion: Can the portal work if the proof service disappears, and how?
milestones.failureDrill: Serve a stale manifest or wrong-chain root to the client.
milestones.defense: Verify a claim using only the published dataset and contract state.

milestones.title: D5 · Administration & adversarial review
milestones.objective: Threat-model the distribution pipeline and test privileged changes.
deliverables: Invariant tests plus one realistic exploit report

criteria.text: Root replacement and funding authority are explicit
Reentrant and duplicate claim sequences preserve accounting
The report separates proof validity from fairness of the allocation dataset

milestones.designQuestion: What can a compromised manifest publisher do even if proof verification is correct?
milestones.failureDrill: Publish a valid root for a malicious allocation dataset and analyze what users can detect.
milestones.defense: Explain the residual trust model and demonstrate a minimized contract bug fix.

milestones.title: D6 · Release package & signed-claim comparison
milestones.objective: Ship a reproducible distribution and compare the design with signed claims.
deliverables: Testnet deployment and reproducible claim walkthrough
ADR comparing Merkle and EIP-712 authorization

criteria.text: Manifest, deployment and funding totals reconcile
Versioned artifacts allow independent reconstruction
Signed-claim comparison addresses nonce, expiry and domain binding

milestones.designQuestion: At what scale or update frequency would you change authorization models?
milestones.failureDrill: Ask a reviewer to claim from a clean environment using published artifacts alone.
milestones.defense: Design a signed alternative and identify what replay protection it needs beyond EIP-712.

projects.title: Verifiable raffle & randomness operations
projects.brief: Build a round-based raffle with immutable entry snapshots, asynchronous verifiable randomness, settlement, claims and an operator dashboard. The hard part is preserving fairness and liveness through delayed and out-of-order events.
outcomes: Model asynchronous state transitions
Separate randomness fulfillment from payouts
Operate and explain fairness assumptions
projects.readiness: Contract state machines, external callbacks, events and adversarial testing.
projects.scope: Testnet simulation with test funds; no real-money gambling launch. Choose and document one supported VRF integration version.

milestones.title: R1 · Round model, fairness & threat analysis
milestones.objective: Specify entry, locking, randomness, settlement and claims as separate phases.
deliverables: Round state machine and threat model

criteria.text: Eligibility and entries become immutable at the stated boundary
No actor can discard an unfavorable completed draw
Timeout policy does not secretly introduce rerolls

milestones.designQuestion: Which fairness guarantees come from the randomness source and which from your state machine?
milestones.failureDrill: Consider an operator observing an unfavorable result and withholding settlement.
milestones.defense: Explain why timestamp or block data alone is unsuitable for this threat model.

milestones.title: R2 · Entry accounting & round locking
milestones.objective: Implement entry limits, deterministic snapshots and round isolation.

criteria.text: Entrants cannot change a locked round
Round liabilities and fees reconcile with supported funds
Unbounded entrant loops are absent from required settlement paths

milestones.designQuestion: How can the winner be selected without iterating over every entrant on chain?
milestones.failureDrill: Enter at the locking boundary and force extra ETH into the contract.
milestones.defense: Derive the relationship between tickets, collected funds and prize liability.

milestones.title: R3 · VRF request lifecycle & callbacks
milestones.objective: Integrate verifiable randomness with durable request-to-round identity and minimal fulfillment work.

criteria.text: Each fulfillment resolves only its recorded request/round
Inputs remain frozen after requesting randomness
Callback stores the result with bounded work; payout failure cannot break fulfillment

milestones.designQuestion: What must be persisted before issuing the external request?
milestones.failureDrill: Fulfill requests in reverse order, delay one, and simulate unavailable funding.
milestones.defense: Trace two concurrent rounds and show why fulfillment order cannot change their entrants.

milestones.title: R4 · Settlement, claims & failure isolation
milestones.objective: Settle a known result and let the winner claim without blocking later rounds.
deliverables: Winner proof and immutable round history

criteria.text: Settlement is repeat-safe and cannot choose a new result
A failing recipient cannot block unrelated rounds
Claims and remaining liabilities reconcile after every action

milestones.designQuestion: Should settlement be permissionless, automated or operator initiated, and why?
milestones.failureDrill: Make the winner a contract that rejects payment, then process the next round.
milestones.defense: Explain why retrying settlement is different from requesting fresh randomness.

milestones.title: R5 · Participant UI & operator control room
milestones.objective: Expose round status and uncertainty to participants and operators.
deliverables: Entry/history UI and indexed round timeline

criteria.text: Submitted entry is not shown as eligible until observed under the declared policy
Users can distinguish waiting for randomness from waiting for settlement
Operator controls expose authority and cannot override a completed result

milestones.designQuestion: Which operational metric detects a stuck round before a participant reports it?
milestones.failureDrill: Take the indexer offline while a request is pending and recover from chain history.
milestones.defense: Diagnose a delayed round from its event timeline without inspecting implementation first.
topicTitles: Reading event logs on the frontend

milestones.title: R6 · Adversarial campaign & fairness defense
milestones.objective: Validate the entire asynchronous system and publish a reproducible case study.
deliverables: Stateful test campaign and failure matrix
Testnet demo, runbook and fairness limitations

criteria.text: Reordered actions cannot double-pay or reopen entry
Funding/confirmation assumptions are documented for the chosen network
Independent reviewer can reproduce a delayed-round recovery

milestones.designQuestion: What reorganization risk remains and how did it influence confirmation policy?
milestones.failureDrill: Inject a request-ID mixup and show the test that detects the wrong winner.
milestones.defense: Defend fairness, authority and liveness separately; implement one unseen round-rule change.
